Thanks again for a productive call earlier — quick recap and clear next steps so we can keep momentum: 

What we covered (high level)
- Scope: build an embedding-backed product search + reranker, then add structured tool-calling for fulfillment actions.
- Initial perf targets: p95 generation < 300ms for short prompts, embedding latency < 50ms for batch lookups.
- Architecture: Redwood hosted for pilot, Dedicated or Private for long-term production; local SDK + sample apps for dev.

Immediate next steps (we can triage these on the tech deep-dive)
1) Redwood team: share SDK quickstart playbook + sample repo (attached + link below).
2) Lumina: confirm who will be the technical lead for the deep-dive (Priya?).
3) Prep items: sample dataset for embeddings (CSV), handful of product prompts, and any redlines for security/retention.

Quicknotes for your engineers (short checklist)
- SDKs: Python and TypeScript clients are available; minimal env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENDPOINT, REDWOOD_REGION.
- Local testing: we provide a local dev mode for SDKs that proxies to hosted models (no full-model download required). If you want to run model weights locally, you'll need >=16GB GPU and follow our Private deployment docs.
- Routing: you can pin routes by latency/cost/region; we'll share example route policy JSON in the repo.
- Structured output / function-calling: we recommend JSON schema-first for predictable parsing; sample function schemas are in the repo.

Attachments: sdks_quickstart_playbook.pdf (quick commands + code snippets), sample app repo link below.

I'll drop the sample repo and playbook links below and loop Marissa (SE) for the deep technical follow-up.

Links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/lumina-samples

Thanks,

Hi Sam / Priya — Marissa (SE) here, following up with concrete quickstart steps and minimal examples you can run in a dev laptop. I attached the playbook but pasted the most-requested bits below so you can copy/paste.

ENVIRONMENT & AUTH
- Required env vars (CI-friendly names):
  - REDWOOD_API_KEY=redw_live_xxx (store in vault/CI secrets)
  - REDWOOD_ENDPOINT=https://api.redwood.inference
  - REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2
  - REDWOOD_MODEL=gpt-redwood-1-4b (override per-route)
- Local dev proxy: set REDWOOD_LOCAL_PROXY=true and REDWOOD_PROXY_ADDR=http://localhost:8000. In this mode the SDK forwards requests to the hosted endpoint through a local auth shim — no model binaries are downloaded. To run fully offline (model-in-memory) you must deploy Redwood Private and pull weights (advanced).

PYTHON QUICKSTART (venv)
pip install redwood-client

python example:
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'], endpoint=os.environ['REDWOOD_ENDPOINT'])
# generation
gen = client.generate(prompt="Find matching products for 'wireless headphones'", model=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_MODEL'))
print(gen.text)

# function-calling / structured output (schema-first)
func_schema = {"name":"place_order","params":{"type":"object","properties":{"sku":{"type":"string"},"qty":{"type":"integer"}}}}
resp = client.generate(prompt="Place order for user", functions=[func_schema], function_call="auto")
print(resp.function_call)

TYPESCRIPT QUICKSTART (node 18+)
npm install @redwood-ai/client

import Redwood from '@redwood-ai/client'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, endpoint: process.env.REDWOOD_ENDPOINT })
const out = await client.generate({ prompt: 'Summarize product features', model: process.env.REDWOOD_MODEL })
console.log(out.text)

ROUTING / FALLBACK EXAMPLE (policy snippet)
{
  "route_policy": "latency_first",
  "preferred_models": ["gpt-redwood-1-4b"],
  "fallback_models": ["gpt-redwood-1-2b-quant"],
  "max_latency_ms": 400
}

EMBEDDINGS + RERANKER
- Default sample embeddings in the repo use 1536 dimensions (open-compatible) unless you pick a smaller, quantized profile.
- We recommend building an approximate-nearest-neighbor index (FAISS/HNSW) and then running a lightweight transformer reranker on top (we include a minimal reranker in the samples).

LOCAL TESTING NOTES
- Local proxy mode: minimal firewall changes (outbound to Redwood required) unless you host the proxy inside your VPC.
- If you want to run the end-to-end latency tests locally without cloud calls, spin up our local-playground container (docker-compose provided). It emulates routing and logs but still requires the API_KEY for auth.

ATTACHMENTS & REPOS
- sdks_quickstart_playbook.pdf (attached) — full commands, sample env files, troubleshooting.
- Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/lumina-samples — contains a Python app (examples/python/app.py) and a TS app (examples/ts/server.ts) with small test harnesses.

If helpful, I can paste a minimal TS test script here or drop a short Gist.

-Marissa
